result:
I fixed the bug, but I haven't confirmed it against your exact scenario, and I didn't add a regression test. The full suite gives 1119 passed and 1 failed, and the one failure is `tests/test_config.py::test_editable_fields_live_editable_fields`. It fails the same way with my change stashed, so it isn't caused by the fix.

**Cause:** the routing tier cache was keyed only by session plus a hash of the conversation's first user message. Your sonnet turn and your opus turn share that key, so the haiku result from the sonnet turn was stored under it. When the opus turn had no fresh text to classify, it replayed that cached haiku. The replay paths either skip the cap entirely (tool-result continuations, bare "yes" affirmations) or only block upgrades, so nothing stopped the downgrade.

**Fix:** in `anthrouter/handlers.py` (`_prepare`), the tier cache key now also includes the requested model. A turn requested as opus can then only reuse tiers cached from earlier opus-requested turns. The size-floor context tracking still uses the original key.

I haven't traced the exact path your opus turn took. It could be any of the three replay paths (text-less turn, tool-result continuation, or affirmation), and they all read the same cache key.
